text:
priya: Heads-up — customer AcmeBank wants a 2-week runway for holiday traffic in their private VPC. They expect 3x baseline peak qps during promo week. Need recommendations for GPU hours and safety buffer.

alex: Got it. Do we have their current baseline numbers (qps, avg seq len, model variant)?

priya: Baseline peak qps = 120 req/s, avg seq len = 220 tokens, using rdm-gpt-xl-16k (fp16). They want <150ms p95.

sam: Quick sanity calc: token/s = 120 * 220 = 26,400 tok/s. If model throughput on a single A100-80GB is ~80 tok/s (steady-state generation), that's ~330 GPU-seconds/s -> ~0.0917 GPUs needed continuously. But with 3x peak and headroom + batch inefficiencies, multiply by ~10.

kevin: Let's put that in a small calc so ops can vet.

sam: ```
# rough per-second GPU equivalents
baseline_qps=120
avg_tokens=220
tokens_per_sec=baseline_qps*avg_tokens # 26400
model_throughput_tok_per_gpu=8000 # assumed throughput per GPU (tokens/sec)
# GPUs needed = tokens_per_sec / model_throughput_tok_per_gpu
# baseline -> 3.3 GPUs, 3x peak -> ~10 GPUs, add 20% headroom -> 12 GPUs
```

priya: Wait model_throughput_tok_per_gpu=8000 seems high for autoregressive decode. Are you assuming batching with sequence parallelism?

sam: Yeah that was for batched batched decode with quantized kernel on H100. For A100 real numbers are lower. Updated numbers: 2500 tok/s per A100 conservative.

kevin: Using 2500 tok/s: baseline 26400/2500 ~ 10.6 GPUs. 3x peak -> ~32 GPUs. Add 25% headroom -> 40 GPUs. That matches what we saw in earlier customer POCs.

alex: Also need to account for KV cache memory per session. AcmeBank has long chat sessions -> KV retention increases memory pressure, so fewer inference instances per GPU. Suggest reducing packing factor by 20% for safety.

priya: Good call. Packing factor and cold-start burst influence the runway. They want two-week guarantee with daily peaks at 3x and intermittent bursts at 5x for new promo events.

kevin: Network note: their VPC sits in us-east-1 with a 10Gb transit gateway. If we scale to 40 GPUs across 3 racks, egress for responses could saturate network during big bursts. Recommend validating NIC and TOR oversubscription.

tess: On procurement lead time — customers typically order pods size N x 8x A100 nodes. Long-lead for GPUs is 10-16 weeks. If customer wants guaranteed capacity by Nov 15, procurement must start by end of July.

priya: Ops ask: what's recommended committed capacity vs on-demand burst mix? We want to minimize cost but meet SLOs.

sam: My recommendation: commit 60% as Dedicated (for predictable baseline + 2x baseline headroom) and allow 40% on-demand/partner-burst for promo spikes (which we route to compatible quantized variants). That gives cost predictability and runway.

kevin: Also propose autoscaling cooldowns of 2m for scale-up, 10m for scale-down to avoid oscillation during promo traffic. Use request-based scaling with observed token/sec per instance.

alex: For the customer sizing doc, include a simple table of scenarios (baseline, 3x peak, 5x burst) with GPU counts, CPU cores per node, RAM, rack power.

priya: I'll draft the customer-facing pod sizing guide. Short checklist: 1) Confirm model variant & quantization options 2) Confirm avg seq_len and session KV retention 3) Confirm peak multipliers and burst durations 4) Network egress validation 5) Procurement lead time 6) SLA for capacity switchovers.

tess: Tagging infra-bot for a quick capacity feasibility check. @infra-bot can you run a regional pod availability check for us-east-1 for 40 A100 80GB equivalents?

infra-bot: Running availability check... estimated fulfillment: 28 A100 nodes available in 6-8 weeks; additional 12 nodes require 10-14 weeks lead time. (this is a simulated check)

kevin: That means we should push for a hybrid approach: reserve 28 now and plan for partner-burst/supplemental quantized routing for the remainder. Also discuss fallbacks in Redwood Console for model downgrade with graceful latency/cost trade-off.

priya: OK action items: - I will update customer with 28-node immediate reserve + plan for additional 12 nodes in 12 weeks. - Alex + Sam, help me draft the rack/power/network checklist. - Tess, include procurement timeline and contract language for capacity guarantees.

alex: I'll paste a mini check snippet for the checklist:```
Rack power per node: 3.5kW
CPU: 64 vCPU
RAM: 512GB
NIC: 2x25GbE (bonded)
Storage: 1TB NVMe for model cache
```

sam: Also include a note: schedule a dry-run traffic spike test (10% of expected peak) two weeks before promo.

priya: Thanks all. I'll circulate the draft sizing doc later today and tag for review. :thumbsup:
